recentItems.title: Who can afford to give up the Donbas most? | DW News
recentItems.description:
Could the Donbas region be the key to ending the war in Ukraine? The Ukrainian territory, made up of Donetsk and Luhansk, has seen some of the bloodiest fighting of Russia's war. But both sides are refusing to walk away because of its critical military value, centuries-long economic history, and political importance. We will take a closer look at Ukraine's Fortress Belt and explore the value of high ground in the age of drones. We find out who can afford to give up the Donbas, taking a closer look at the origins of the conflict, Vladimir Putin's stake, and Volodymyr Zelenskyy's refusal to make territorial concessions. Through a military, economic and political scorecard, we answer the critical question: who needs the Donbas more, and could it unlock a future peace deal?

recentItems.title: Why the non-Western 'talking club' for China, Russia and India matters | DW News
recentItems.description:
China’s Xi Jinping, Russia's Vladimir Putin, and India’s Narendra Modi are among the powerful leaders who show up to the Shanghai Cooperation Organization — even though its summits often produce few concrete results. So why does the SCO matter, and why are more countries interested in joining? DW's Melissa Chan speaks with experts Eva Seiwert of MERICS and Temur Umarov of the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center about how the 25-year-old organization has become a platform for geopolitical signaling, China's push for an alternative to US-led institutions, and how countries like India and the Central Asian states use the meeting to navigate an increasingly complicated world.

recentItems.title: Why a seized Russian ship is reigniting tensions in Svalbard | DW News
recentItems.description:
A Russian ship has been seized in the Arctic, sparking accusations of piracy from Moscow and opening a new front in a legal battle that began with the annexation of Crimea. So why is Norway enforcing a multi-billion-dollar ruling against Russia now, and why has the remote archipelago of Svalbard become the center of the dispute? We break down the law, the politics and how the Ukraine war is playing out in the Far North with Arctic security analyst Marisol Maddox.
